media.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of Henri-Georges Clouzot in profile.
media.publicCaption: Henri-Georges Clouzot, credited as director of Tout pour l’amour in 1933. The portrait is later: Studio Harcourt photographed him in 1947, the year of Quai des Orfèvres.
media.publicCreditLine: Studio Harcourt, 1947; Réunion des musées nationaux; Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared, and the public-domain tag carried by the Wikimedia Commons file is not relied on here. The photograph was made by Studio Harcourt in 1947 and is distributed by the Réunion des musées nationaux, which licenses it commercially. As a French collective work its term runs seventy years from publication, so it was still protected in France on 1 January 1996, the United States restoration date, and the URAA therefore restored United States copyright for ninety-five years from publication. A reduced-resolution reproduction (360 × 489 px, from 479 × 650 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
